def date_diagnostics(df, name):
    print(f"\n📊 {name}")
    print("Date range:", df["date"].min(), "→", df["date"].max())
    print("Total days:", df["date"].nunique())
    print("Duplicate dates:", df["date"].duplicated().sum())

date_diagnostics(core_enrol_df, "Core Enrollment Features")
date_diagnostics(adv_enrol_df, "Advanced Enrollment Features")

# Cell 2B-6: Rolling volatility and stability signals (7-day window)

daily_core["rolling_mean_7d"] = (
    daily_core["total_enrolments"]
    .rolling(window=7, min_periods=3)
    .mean()
)

daily_core["rolling_std_7d"] = (
    daily_core["total_enrolments"]
    .rolling(window=7, min_periods=3)
    .std()
)

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import mplcursors
import matplotlib.dates as mdates

# 🎨 Refined pastel dashboard palette
PURPLE = "#7B6ED6"
LAVENDER = "#CDB4DB"
PINK = "#FFAFCC"
GRID = "#EADCF5"
TEXT = "#4B3F72"

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 6))

# Main line (clean & confident)
line, = ax.plot(
    daily_core["date"],
    daily_core["total_enrolments"],
    color=PURPLE,
    linewidth=3,
    alpha=0.95
)

# Soft area fill (lighter & airy)
ax.fill_between(
    daily_core["date"],
    daily_core["total_enrolments"],
    color=LAVENDER,
    alpha=0.35
)

# Titles
ax.set_title(
    "System-Level Aadhaar Enrollments Over Time",
    fontsize=17,
    fontweight="bold",
    color=TEXT,
    pad=18
)

ax.set_xlabel("Date", fontsize=11, color=TEXT)
ax.set_ylabel("Total Enrolments", fontsize=11, color=TEXT)

# Grid
ax.grid(
    True,
    linestyle="--",
    linewidth=0.6,
    color=GRID,
    alpha=0.9
)

# Clean spines
for spine in ["top", "right"]:
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["left"].set_color(GRID)
ax.spines["bottom"].set_color(GRID)

ax.tick_params(colors=TEXT)

# Improve date formatting
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.AutoDateLocator())
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.ConciseDateFormatter(ax.xaxis.get_major_locator()))

# ✨ Hover interaction (clean + readable)
cursor = mplcursors.cursor(line, hover=True)

@cursor.connect("add")
def on_add(sel):
    x, y = sel.target
    sel.annotation.set_text(
        f"Date: {mdates.num2date(x).strftime('%d %b %Y')}\n"
        f"Enrolments: {int(y):,}"
    )
    sel.annotation.get_bbox_patch().set(
        fc="white",
        ec=PURPLE,
        lw=1.2,
        alpha=0.95
    )

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# 🎨 Pastel dashboard palette
RAW_COLOR   = "#F48FB1"   # soft pink
TREND_COLOR = "#7B6ED6"   # purple
FILL_COLOR  = "#CDB4DB"   # lavender
GRID_COLOR  = "#EADCF5"
TEXT_COLOR  = "#4B3F72"

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 6))

# --- Pink gradient under RAW line (layered fills) ---
gradient_levels = np.linspace(0.15, 0.45, 6)

for alpha in gradient_levels:
    ax.fill_between(
        daily_core["date"],
        daily_core["total_enrolments"],
        color=RAW_COLOR,
        alpha=alpha / 10
    )

# Raw daily enrolments (THICKER & visible)
ax.plot(
    daily_core["date"],
    daily_core["total_enrolments"],
    color=RAW_COLOR,
    linewidth=3.2,
    alpha=0.9,
    label="Daily Enrolments"
)

# 7-day trend (dominant purple)
ax.plot(
    daily_core["date"],
    daily_core["rolling_7d"],
    color=TREND_COLOR,
    linewidth=3.8,
    alpha=0.95,
    label="7-Day Trend"
)

# Lavender fill under trend
ax.fill_between(
    daily_core["date"],
    daily_core["rolling_7d"],
    color=FILL_COLOR,
    alpha=0.35
)

# Titles & labels
ax.set_title(
    "Aadhaar Enrolments: Daily vs 7-Day Trend",
    fontsize=17,
    fontweight="bold",
    color=TEXT_COLOR,
    pad=14
)

ax.set_xlabel("Date", fontsize=11, color=TEXT_COLOR)
ax.set_ylabel("Number of Enrolments", fontsize=11, color=TEXT_COLOR)

# Grid
ax.grid(
    True,
    linestyle="--",
    linewidth=0.6,
    color=GRID_COLOR,
    alpha=0.9
)

# Clean axes
ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["left"].set_color(GRID_COLOR)
ax.spines["bottom"].set_color(GRID_COLOR)

ax.tick_params(colors=TEXT_COLOR)

# Legend
ax.legend(frameon=False)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Colour palette (dashboard theme)
LINE_COLOR   = "#7B1FA2"   # deep purple
LOW_COLOR    = "#F3E5F5"   # very light lavender
MID_COLOR    = "#CE93D8"   # soft purple
HIGH_COLOR   = "#F48FB1"   # pink highlight
GRID_COLOR   = "#E0E0E0"
TEXT_COLOR   = "#263238"

# Thresholds (adjust if needed)
LOW_TH  = daily_core["volatility_index"].quantile(0.33)
HIGH_TH = daily_core["volatility_index"].quantile(0.66)

plt.figure(figsize=(14, 6))

# Background threshold bands
plt.axhspan(
    0, LOW_TH,
    color=LOW_COLOR,
    alpha=0.9,
    label="Low Volatility (Stable)"
)

plt.axhspan(
    LOW_TH, HIGH_TH,
    color=MID_COLOR,
    alpha=0.65,
    label="Medium Volatility (Friction)"
)

plt.axhspan(
    HIGH_TH, daily_core["volatility_index"].max() * 1.1,
    color=HIGH_COLOR,
    alpha=0.5,
    label="High Volatility (Saturation)"
)

# Main volatility line
plt.plot(
    daily_core["date"],
    daily_core["volatility_index"],
    color=LINE_COLOR,
    linewidth=3
)

# Title & labels
plt.title(
    "System Volatility Index Over Time",
    fontsize=17,
    fontweight="bold",
    color=TEXT_COLOR,
    pad=12
)

plt.xlabel("Date", fontsize=11, color=TEXT_COLOR)
plt.ylabel("Volatility Index", fontsize=11, color=TEXT_COLOR)

# Grid & styling
plt.grid(
    True,
    linestyle="--",
    linewidth=0.6,
    color=GRID_COLOR
)

ax = plt.gca()
ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
ax.tick_params(colors=TEXT_COLOR)

plt.legend(frameon=False, ncol=3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Theme colours
LOW_COLOR    = "#F3E5F5"   # lavender (stable)
MID_COLOR    = "#CE93D8"   # purple (friction)
HIGH_COLOR   = "#F48FB1"   # pink (saturation)
POINT_EDGE   = "#4A148C"
TEXT_COLOR   = "#263238"
GRID_COLOR   = "#E0E0E0"

# Thresholds (same logic as volatility plot)
LOW_TH  = daily_core["volatility_index"].quantile(0.33)
HIGH_TH = daily_core["volatility_index"].quantile(0.66)

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

# Regime masks
stable = daily_core["volatility_index"] <= LOW_TH
friction = (daily_core["volatility_index"] > LOW_TH) & (daily_core["volatility_index"] <= HIGH_TH)
saturation = daily_core["volatility_index"] > HIGH_TH

# Scatter plots by regime
plt.scatter(
    daily_core.loc[stable, "total_enrolments"],
    daily_core.loc[stable, "volatility_index"],
    color=LOW_COLOR,
    edgecolor=POINT_EDGE,
    alpha=0.85,
    s=60,
    label="Stable Regime"
)

plt.scatter(
    daily_core.loc[friction, "total_enrolments"],
    daily_core.loc[friction, "volatility_index"],
    color=MID_COLOR,
    edgecolor=POINT_EDGE,
    alpha=0.85,
    s=60,
    label="Friction Regime"
)

plt.scatter(
    daily_core.loc[saturation, "total_enrolments"],
    daily_core.loc[saturation, "volatility_index"],
    color=HIGH_COLOR,
    edgecolor=POINT_EDGE,
    alpha=0.85,
    s=70,
    label="Saturation Regime"
)

# Horizontal threshold lines
plt.axhline(LOW_TH, color="#9575CD", linestyle="--", linewidth=1)
plt.axhline(HIGH_TH, color="#EC407A", linestyle="--", linewidth=1)

# Titles & labels
plt.title(
    "Enrollment Volume vs System Volatility",
    fontsize=17,
    fontweight="bold",
    color=TEXT_COLOR,
    pad=12
)

plt.xlabel("Total Enrolments", fontsize=11, color=TEXT_COLOR)
plt.ylabel("Volatility Index", fontsize=11, color=TEXT_COLOR)

# Grid & axes styling
plt.grid(True, linestyle="--", linewidth=0.6, color=GRID_COLOR)

ax = plt.gca()
ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
ax.tick_params(colors=TEXT_COLOR)

plt.legend(frameon=False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Dashboard colour palette
NORMAL_COLOR = "#8E24AA"   # lavender (normal)
STRESS_COLOR = "#EC407A"   # strong pink (stress)
GRID_COLOR   = "#E0E0E0"
TEXT_COLOR   = "#263238"

plt.figure(figsize=(14, 4))

# Separate normal vs stress days
normal_days = daily_core["stress_flag"] == 0
stress_days = daily_core["stress_flag"] == 1

# Normal days (background context)
plt.scatter(
    daily_core.loc[normal_days, "date"],
    daily_core.loc[normal_days, "stress_flag"].astype(int),
    color=NORMAL_COLOR,
    s=40,
    alpha=0.6,
    label="Normal Days"
)

# High-stress days (emphasized)
plt.scatter(
    daily_core.loc[stress_days, "date"],
    daily_core.loc[stress_days, "stress_flag"].astype(int),
    color=STRESS_COLOR,
    s=80,
    alpha=0.9,
    label="High-Stress Days"
)

# Title & labels
plt.title(
    "High-Stress Days (Discrete Events)",
    fontsize=16,
    fontweight="bold",
    color=TEXT_COLOR,
    pad=10
)
plt.xlabel("Date", fontsize=11, color=TEXT_COLOR)
plt.ylabel("Stress Flag (0 = Normal, 1 = High)", fontsize=11, color=TEXT_COLOR)

# Axis formatting
plt.yticks([0, 1], ["Normal", "High Stress"])

# Grid & cleanup
plt.grid(True, linestyle="--", linewidth=0.6, color=GRID_COLOR)

ax = plt.gca()
ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
ax.tick_params(colors=TEXT_COLOR)

plt.legend(frameon=False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import calendar

# 🎨 Theme colors
LAVENDER = "#CDB4DB"
PURPLE   = "#7B6ED6"
PINK     = "#FFAFCC"
TEXT     = "#4B3F72"
GRID     = "#EADCF5"

# Convert month numbers to names (Jan, Feb, ...)
month_labels = [
    calendar.month_abbr[m] for m in monthly_core["month"]

# Cell 5-1 (FIXED): State-level volume and volatility (behavioral)

# Daily enrollment per state
state_daily = (
    core_enrol_df
    .groupby(["state_clean", "date"], as_index=False)["total_enrolments"]
    .sum()
)

# State-level volume
state_volume = (
    state_daily
    .groupby("state_clean", as_index=False)["total_enrolments"]
    .sum()
    .rename(columns={"total_enrolments": "state_total_enrolments"})
)

# State-level volatility (std / mean across days)
state_volatility = (
    state_daily
    .groupby("state_clean")["total_enrolments"]
    .agg(["mean", "std"])
    .reset_index()
)

state_volatility["state_volatility_index"] = (
    state_volatility["std"] / state_volatility["mean"]
)

# Merge behavior metrics
state_behavior = state_volume.merge(
    state_volatility[["state_clean", "state_volatility_index"]],
    on="state_clean",
    how="left"
)

state_behavior.head()

)

)

# Cell 5-3: Behavioral typology segmentation (volume × volatility)

# Define thresholds using medians (robust to skew)
volume_thresh = state_behavior["state_total_enrolments"].median()
volatility_thresh = state_behavior["state_volatility_index"].median()

def classify_region(row):
    if row["state_total_enrolments"] >= volume_thresh and row["state_volatility_index"] < volatility_thresh:
        return "High Volume – Stable (Mature)"
    elif row["state_total_enrolments"] >= volume_thresh and row["state_volatility_index"] >= volatility_thresh:
        return "High Volume – Volatile (Strained)"
    elif row["state_total_enrolments"] < volume_thresh and row["state_volatility_index"] >= volatility_thresh:
        return "Low Volume – Volatile (Fragile)"
    else:
        return "Low Volume – Stable"

state_behavior["behavior_type"] = state_behavior.apply(classify_region, axis=1)

state_behavior["behavior_type"].value_counts()

        "Low Volume – Volatile (Fragile)"
    ])) &
    (decision_summary["stress_day_count"] > 0)
]

priority_regions[["state_clean", "behavior_type", "stress_day_count"]]
